raw:
The library door closes behind you on the dining hall’s last clink of silver. Lamp oil and old paper hang in the warm air. Open shelves rise along both walls beneath the upper gallery, their brass labels arranged by institutions, eras, and legal categories rather than anything as useful as “start here.”

The Council section offers *Collected Petitions of the Ninth Session*, *Maritime Arbitration Precedents*, and three dense volumes of treaty commentary. None looks likely to explain what a Council actually does before assuming you already know.

At a desk beneath the iron spiral stair, a man in a worn black academic coat is making notes in a ledger with a blue pencil. A small plaque identifies him as Professor Gareth Stone, Human Covenant History.

When you ask for an introduction, he sets the pencil down.

“Try this first.” He crosses to a lower shelf and draws out a slim, dark-blue volume. *The Council in Practice: An Orientation for New Delegates.* “It explains the seats, voting rules, committees, and the Academy’s part in all of it. Read the committee chapter before the procedure chapter. Most matters are decided long before anyone gives a formal speech.”

He hands it over without lingering over your signet or surname.

The book is plainly bound but well used, its margins crowded with generations of students’ notes. A paper marker rests at the opening chapter: *The Seven Seats and Their Obligations.*
